#!/bin/bash
# the engineer's new unit tests, through the heavy slot; result in out-new.txt, "exit=" last
cd /home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-116 || exit 2
bash .gov-runtime/scratch/eng/pt.sh tests/unit/rebuild/test_w2_116_when_due.py \
  tests/unit/status/test_w2_116_integration_store.py tests/unit/retrieval/test_w2_116_token_mark.py \
  > .gov-runtime/scratch/eng/out-new.txt 2>&1
echo "exit=$?" >> .gov-runtime/scratch/eng/out-new.txt

(b) `git hash-object -w` (`1ae28402a109`) and `git update-index --refresh` both exited 0. `GOV_TICKET=DAEO-f58b`. `ps -eo pid,args | grep -iE "[o]llama|[l]lama-server"` showed nothing of mine, and I started no embedder, reranker or model.

- **task:** DAEO-f58b (W2-116) pass 2b: S2 (`--when-due`, `gov status`'s `integration_store` part) and R2-F3
- **status:** ESCALATION. The lead's `HOLD` file appeared at 18:44 and was still there at 19:14, past my 20-minute limit. No merge has started. I stopped editing and committing and found one bug I could not fix.
- **work_completed:**
  - **R2-F3, built and committed (batch 1).** The token carries `f`, the store folder as resolved once. A token on another folder is refused `CONTINUATION_INVALID` even at the same commit. The message names both folders and `details` has `token_root` and `store_root`. A token with no mark is refused. The commit check still runs first, so W2-138's messages and details are unchanged.
  - **S2 core, written and uncommitted, in `integration.py` and `command.py`.** It has:
    - the `integration_refresh` reader with `REBUILD_CONFIG_INVALID` (`key` and `value` in `details`);
    - the `GOV_NOW` clock, `--when-due` and its due rules;
    - `<link>.refresh.json`, written whole by atomic replace, with `at` the time the decision was taken;
    - the `not_due` result, and `last_due` for the status part.
  - **`gov status`'s `integration_store` part, written and uncommitted.** It is in the new `src/gov/status/integration_store.py`, wired into `command.py` with the docstring updated to eight parts. Where a figure cannot be read, `stale` is `{"read": false}` rather than `false`. A reason that holds is still reported even when another check is unread.
  - **This repository's `integration_refresh` line is in `governance/project/rebuild.yaml`.** I checked every reader of that file for a check that refuses unknown keys, and none does:
    - `config.loader._rebuild_settings` checks `REBUILD_FLAGS` only;
    - `rebuild.watch.settings` reads `slow_after_s` and `lock`;
    - `rebuild.seed._configured` and `memaudit.schedule.store_link` read `integration_store`;
    - `launch.store.configured` reads `integration_store`;
    - `lexical` only stamps the file, so editing it makes the lexical index stale once, which is expected.
  - **The evidence record's "Pass 2b" section is not written.**
- **files_changed:**
  - **Committed:** `src/gov/retrieval/retrieve.py`, `tests/unit/retrieval/test_w2_116_token_mark.py`.
  - **Uncommitted:** `src/gov/rebuild/integration.py`, `src/gov/rebuild/command.py`, `src/gov/status/command.py`, `src/gov/status/integration_store.py` (new), `governance/project/rebuild.yaml`, `tests/unit/rebuild/test_w2_116_when_due.py` (new), `tests/unit/status/test_w2_116_integration_store.py` (new).
- **evidence:** every run went through `heavy_slot.sh`.
  - `tests/unit/retrieval/test_w2_116_token_mark.py` plus `test_w2_138_store.py`: **20 passed**, run before the commit.
  - The three new unit files together: **56 passed, 3 failed**, 76 deselected, run during the hold. This run included the token tests, so the 56 passes include the token file's passes.
  - `tests/unit/status` before my new files: 12 passed, 1 failed (`test_status.py`, below).
  - **Not run:** the whole folders `tests/unit/rebuild`, `status`, `retrieval`, `retrieve`, and `tests/acceptance/W2-116/`. Nothing in this pass has run against the designer's cases yet.
- **tests:**
  - **Three failures in my uncommitted files, two causes.**
    - `test_gov_now_with_an_offset_is_that_instant_and_that_wall_clock` and `test_due_runs_the_refresh_names_its_reason_and_writes_the_record_whole` fail on a bug in `integration.now()` (see risks).
    - `test_without_gov_now_it_is_the_real_clock` fails on a test bug: `monkeypatch.delenv("GOV_NOW")` needs `raising=False`.
  - **One existing case now red by the interface.** `tests/unit/status/test_status.py:172` (`test_a_status_with_a_part_not_read_names_every_such_place`) asserts the exact `PARTS` tuple and `not_read == []`. The interface requires the new part, and a project with no `integration_store` lists it in `not_read`. The file is outside my paths and I did not touch it. Its `PARTS` needs `"integration_store"`, and its project needs a store or an expected `not_read` entry.
  - The known reds (three `test_cto_safety_nets.py` live-inbox cases, `test_w2_23_space.py:94`) have not been reached.
- **discoveries:**
  - **`/tmp/w2-116-eng` cannot be created.** `/tmp` is read-only in this sandbox, so pytest runs on the sandbox's own `TMPDIR` as the common rules allow.
  - **`heavy_slot.sh` prints a harmless error.** It cannot append to its waits log (`heavy-slot-waits.jsonl: Read-only file system`).
  - **Gate wait.** The gate was full for more than 15 minutes at 18:13–18:49, which I treated as a wait.
  - **A nested `( … ) &` job dies with its shell,** so background runs must use the tool's own background mode.
  - **Denied calls.** The Write tool and one compound Bash call were refused under `.gov-runtime/scratch/eng/`. They were different calls, each tried once, and I used a plain heredoc instead.
  - **Interface gap.** The record keeps only the last refresh. After an `after_nightly` at 10:00 and a `second` at 18:00, the record's reason is `second`. The literal rule, no `after_nightly` record dated today, then makes one more cheap `after_nightly` refresh due at the next tick. It finds the head unchanged, rewrites the record and then stops. Fixing it would need an extra record key or a second file, which the interface does not allow, so I built the literal rule and pinned it in a test.
- **risks:**
  - **`integration.now()` bug.** For a `GOV_NOW` with an offset it ends with `.astimezone()`, which converts to local time. `10:00+01:00` is read as 09:00 UTC, so `at_time` uses the wrong wall clock and a refresh falls due an hour early. On a machine at UTC offset 0 it hides unless an offset is planted. The fix is ready but not applied: keep the parsed value when it carries an offset, and call `.astimezone()` only when it is naive.
  - **Hold-state exposure.** Five edited tracked files and two new source and test files are uncommitted. No merge is in progress, but a merge by the lead into this tree should be done knowing they are there.
- **lessons:** a test that plants an offset in the clock found a bug that a UTC-only sandbox hides.
- **proposed_decisions:** none.
- **unresolved:**
  - **`HOLD` was not lifted within my 20 minutes.** Please lift it or confirm the merge is under way.
  - **`test_status.py:172`** needs a revision by whoever owns it (see tests).
  - **The config `branch` is not checked against the `--integration <branch>` argument.** The interface does not say which wins; I build the command-line branch and `gov status` reads the config's.
  - **Unstated points, my choices:**
    - An empty `GOV_NOW` is invalid.
    - A missing `after_nightly` block is reported as key `integration_refresh.after_nightly.latest` with value null.
    - A present `after_nightly` that is not a map is reported as key `integration_refresh.after_nightly` with the value read.
    - The newest verdict file counts only if its time is at or before `now`; a verdict stamped after `now` is not yet a time that fell due.
    - A record with no readable `at` is treated as no record.
- **recommended_next_action:** lift `HOLD`, or tell me the merge is done. Then I will apply the pending fixes (`.gov-runtime/scratch/eng/checkpoint.txt` has the exact change), rerun the new files and the five folders (`tests/unit/rebuild`, `status`, `retrieval`, `retrieve`, `tests/acceptance/W2-116/`), commit S2 with the yaml line, then status, then write the evidence section, and return with the full counts.
